text: 🧠 Idiocracy turns 20. It was right about everything except the timeline. Mike Judge gave President Camacho 500 years to emerge. We're speedrunning it in real time. The film's sharpest joke isn't the Brawndo ads or the toilet humor, it's that Camacho actually listened to an expert when it counted. That's the detail that stings most in 2026. Idiocracy didn't predict collapse or dictatorship. It predicted a world that stays just functional enough to keep humiliating itself, and somehow that's the scarier outcome. ✈️ Add to watchlist

🍿 Pokémon: Wild Card is real, and the poster already hits different 📆 Estreno: 2027 🎭 Género: #Animation #Adventure ✈️ Add to watchlist Seven years since Detective Pikachu and the franchise skips live-action entirely. Director Katsuhiko Kitada and CloverWorks (of Spy x Family ) are centering a TCG player and Mimikyu. That alone is a more interesting premise than any nostalgia-bait reboot. The poster leans hard cyberpunk: dark palette, sharp angles. For a franchise that lived in pastel comfort for decades, this is a real tonal bet. Cautiously sold.

🍿 Wile E. Coyote almost got deleted. He survived. And the movie is actually good. 📆 Estreno: August 28, 2026 🎭 Género: #Comedy · #Animation · #LiveAction ✈️ Add to watchlist Director Dave Green and Will Forte spent years watching Warners try to bury this thing for a tax write-off. It finally hits theaters, and people are laughing all the way through. Minor miracle. On paper it sounds like a joke. Wile E. takes ACME to court. In practice the heart underneath is real, and you might walk out genuinely moved by a cartoon coyote. The live-action/animation blend earns its nod to Who Framed Roger Rabbit . The movie that nearly didn't exist turns out to be exactly what you needed.

🎃 Other Mommy: the trailer shot that cleared popcorn buckets nationwide 📆 Estreno: October 9, 2026 🎭 Género: #Horror #Thriller ✈️ Add to watchlist Jessica Chastain doing double duty as mom and monster is inspired casting. Josh Malerman's novel has a blue, hairy demon; the film trades it for a doppelganger. A familiar face worn wrong beats any CGI beast. My only question: can it hold that dread past the first act. 🕳️

🍿 Ali G is back. Whether that's good news depends entirely on which Ali G you loved. 📆 Estreno: October 23, 2026 🎭 Género: #Comedy #Mockumentary ✈️ Add to watchlist Sacha Baron Cohen returns as Ali G, now 20 years older and thrown into TikTok culture. The self-aware conceit is genuinely funny. And yes, he directed it himself. The real question is which version shows up. The early Ali G, who exposed establishment cluelessness brilliantly in 'Ali G Indahouse' , or the later one who just leaned into the joke until the joke stopped landing. Picturehouse passing is noise. October 23 is the only verdict that counts.

Chris Hansen bought ads before every screening of his own biopic. That move alone feels like an episode of his show. 📆 Estreno: September 25, 2026 🎭 Género: #Thriller #Drama #Crime ✈️ Add to watchlist Robert Pattinson plays Hansen at the peak of the 2006 To Catch a Predator frenzy. Director Lance Oppenheim has a gift for dissecting the theater of American obsession, and this subject fits him perfectly. Hansen refused to watch the film without a no-lawsuit clause, then bought preshow airtime to frame the story on his own terms. A24 couldn't have scripted better marketing.

🎬 Tim Curry is gone. There was nobody quite like him. Tim Curry died August 26 at 80. Frank-N-Furter in 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show' , Wadsworth in 'Clue' , the Lord of Darkness in 'Legend' . Each role a complete performance, zero filler. Post-stroke, the body slowed. The wit never did. That combination of theatrical precision and gleeful chaos is something film school can't teach and Netflix can't manufacture. RIP. 🎩

🍿 Ali G is back. 24 years later. Make it make sense. 📆 Estreno: October 23, 2026 🎭 Género: #Comedy #Documentary ✈️ Add to watchlist Sacha Baron Cohen wrote, directed and stars in this sequel to 'Ali G Indahouse' , his feature directorial debut via Amazon MGM. The whole thing was shot in secret, which is honestly the most Ali G thing possible. The real question is whether the joke still lands. Prank comedy lives on the target not knowing who you are. Half the world knows Ali G now. The other half has never heard of him and couldn't care less about a parody of early-2000s UK roadman culture. That tension, a character frozen in time facing a world that moved on, could actually be interesting if Cohen leans into it. He probably won't. But the possibility is there.

🍿 Into the Sky: the alien abduction romcom nobody knew they needed 📆 Estreno: September 17, 2026 🎭 Género: #SciFi · #Comedy ✈️ Add to watchlist A guy just wants his wife back. The aliens won't let him. That's the whole pitch, and honestly it sells itself. The premise is absurdist gold, but what makes it land is the casting: Sam Richardson is exactly the kind of actor who makes cosmic humiliation feel warm rather than mean. If you slept on his Werewolves Within , fix that first. This feels like the same DNA: genre scaffolding, genuine heart, jokes that respect your intelligence. Premiering at Fantastic Fest, which tends to have good radar for this stuff.

Destin Daniel Cretton (the guy behind 'Shang-Chi' ) clearly understood what the Sony solo experiments never did: Spider-Man works when Marvel is in the room. Morbius, Madame Web, Kraven... that graveyard exists precisely so this film could feel like a resurrection. Jon Bernthal as Punisher dropping into a Spider-Man film is the kind of swing that only works when there's trust between the studios. Right now, that trust is printing money.

🍿 A billion dollars in four days. Sony is clinging to Peter Parker like their life depends on it. 📆 Estreno: July 31, 2026 🎭 Género: #Action · #Adventure · #Superhero ✈️ Add to watchlist Brand New Day just crossed $1B worldwide in four days, second-fastest ever behind Endgame. Director Destin Daniel Cretton delivered something genuinely grounded for a Holland Spider-Man, and that "I am both" payoff people keep talking about lands harder than any MCU moment in years. Sony killed every solo villain spinoff, kept Spider-Verse 3, and is now riding this wave with everything they've got. Smart. When your one sure thing is this sure, you don't dilute it with Morbius sequels. Tom Holland has now starred in multiple billion-dollar films and counting. At this point he is not just Sony's golden goose, he is the whole farm.

🎬 Ready Player Two is happening, and honestly the book being terrible is the best news possible Zak Penn is officially writing the sequel to 'Ready Player One' , with Spielberg back as producer. Ernest Cline's second novel is, by near-universal agreement, a disaster. Wade becomes an insufferable tech-bro fantasy and the whole thing reads like Elon Musk fan fiction published in 2020. Penn deviated from the first book too, and that's largely why the movie worked. Here he has an even stronger case for throwing out the source material and keeping only the skeleton. The IP is the playground, not the plot. Use it.

🍿 $360 million in three days. Spider-Man just broke everything. Tom Holland and director Destin Daniel Cretton just handed Marvel its biggest opening in history: $360M domestic, edging out 'Avengers: Endgame' after seven years on top. Not a fluke. The top four all-time openings now belong to Marvel. That last part is where it gets interesting for me. Four Marvel titles. Zero surprises in the top four. The genre has basically colonized peak box office like it owns the deed. 'No Way Home' already proved this franchise has no ceiling; Brand New Day just confirmed it has no floor either. 🕷

Street Fighter (2026): Jason Momoa is green. Very, very green. 📆 Estreno: October 16, 2026 🎭 Género: #Action · #VideoGame ✈️ Add to watchlist Kitao Sakurai directing a Street Fighter movie with Jason Momoa as Blanka is exactly the kind of casting that makes you tilt your head and just go with it. Andrew Koji as Ryu is the smarter choice on paper, and the Blanka vs. Ryu sequence has real momentum. The rapid cutting is my main concern, but I'll reserve judgment. 🍿 Avengers: Doomsday — RDJ's back, and he's not playing nice 📆 Estreno: December 18, 2026 🎭 Género: #Action · #SciFi · #Superhero ✈️ Add to watchlist What genuinely intrigues me is Robert Downey Jr. playing Victor Von Doom with a full accent and zero smirk. 🎬 Heat 2 is real. DiCaprio, Bale, Mann. November shoot. After a year of difficult negotiations, DiCaprio and Bale are set to star in Michael Mann 's sequel, filming starting in November. Bale takes Pacino's Vincent Hanna, DiCaprio steps into Kilmer's shoes as Chris Shiherlis. Mann at 83 is taking this globe-trotting production to LA, Chicago, Paraguay, and Singapore. For a director whose last few films barely registered at the box office, this reads like a final, uncompromising statement. The sequel nobody thought would actually happen is happening.

🍿 Suburbia meets the Cretaceous, and somehow nobody knows if that's a comedy 📆 Estreno: August 14, 2026 🎭 Género: #SciFi · #Survival · #Thriller ✈️ Add to watchlist David Robert Mitchell made his bones turning genre rules inside out, from 'It Follows' to the delirious neo-noir of Under the Silver Lake. Now, with Anne Hathaway clutching a porch rifle and Ewan McGregor in angel wings, he gets an $85M studio budget and dinosaurs in the front yard. The tone question is the whole ballgame here. The posters scream dark comedy, the synopsis reads survival horror, and early screenings got laughs. Mitchell playing it straight would intrigue me more than a knowing wink. Either way, this is the most original blockbuster pitch of the summer.

🍿 Backrooms hits PVOD July 7. A24's biggest hit ever, made by a 20-year-old. 📆 Estreno: July 7, 2026 (PVOD) 🎭 Género: #Horror · #SciFi ✈️ Add to watchlist Kane Parsons was 16 when he uploaded a YouTube short about endless fluorescent hallways. Now he's the youngest director to open at number one at the global box office, with $330 million and A24's all-time record. The nightmare logic here isn't a gimmick; it's the whole engine. Chiwetel Ejiofor grounds the disorientation with real weight, and the first two acts are genuinely suffocating. The third act wobbles, sure, but concept-driven horror lives and dies by atmosphere, and this one has it in spades.

🎬 The Magic School Bus is coming to theaters. And yeah, I have concerns. Elizabeth Banks plays Ms. Frizzle, with Rob Letterman writing and directing at Legendary. That combo feels less like education and more like a $150M IP grab with a wacky costume budget. The whole point of this franchise is taking kids on genuinely educational adventures through outer space, the human body, and beyond. Strip that out for quippy one-liners and a "believe in yourself" arc, and the bus is just a cool prop. History says don't hold your breath. 🎒

❗️ Hollywood might be facing its biggest disruption since CGI. A film called Dreams of Violets is set to become the first fully AI-generated movie to premiere at a major festival. It reportedly cost just $2,000 and took two months to make. A similar film made the traditional way could have cost $2–5 million and required a large cast and crew. Meanwhile, Amazon MGM Studios has started experimenting with AI-animated shows, though one project reportedly backed out after public backlash. That’s the big debate: supporters see AI as making filmmaking dramatically cheaper, while critics and unions worry it could replace thousands of creative jobs. A movie for the cost of a used laptop instead of millions of dollars. Hollywood’s economics may never be the same. @aipost 🏴

🍿 Pixar goes mob noir. In Venice. With cats. And it actually looks gorgeous. 📆 Estreno: March 5, 2027 🎭 Género: #Animation · #Comedy · #Adventure ✈️ Add to watchlist The trailer showcases a hand-painted animation style that feels like nothing Pixar has done in years, and that alone is enough to buy my attention. Director Enrico Casarosa returns to Italy after Luca , this time with a scrappy black cat named Nero tangled up in a feline mob. My only real question is whether the music angle gets the space it deserves, or ends up as window dressing on what is already a very full premise.

🎬 RIP Anthony Head, 72. One actor, two completely opposite souls. Anthony Head built his legacy across four very different pillars: Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer , Uther Pendragon in Merlin, and Rupert Mannion in Ted Lasso . What gets me is the range. Giles: the warm father figure every lost kid deserved. Mannion: a smug, hollow villain you pitied as much as you despised. His daughters confirmed he faced complications from pneumonia. He had also lost his longtime partner in 2025. And then there's Repo! The Genetic Opera , the cult gem that deserves its own tribute. Three very different careers in one. All of them real. 🕯

But the IMAX logo on this poster is literally bigger than the title, and those medieval-looking warriors could be from any generic fantasy game cover. 🤨 Matt Damon as Odysseus, with Oppenheimer -level star power behind him. The faith is there. I just hope the film earns an identity as singular as its production. Turn up the subtitles either way.

🍿 Jackass: Best and Last. A farewell that reads like a confession. 📆 Estreno: June 26, 2026 🎭 Género: #Comedy #Stunts #Documentary ✈️ Add to watchlist Johnny Knoxville and director Jeff Tremaine know exactly what this is: a victory lap built on archive gold and a handful of new bits, with no pretense of passing the torch. The new cast isn't on the poster, and that's not an accident. What made Jackass untouchable was never the stunts. It was a specific group of broken, fearless idiots who genuinely loved each other. The film mixes old and new footage, serving as a celebration of the whole franchise. You can't franchise that chemistry, and TikTok proved it by trying every day. Those two empty spaces in the shopping cart poster hit harder than any stunt. Ryan Dunn was part of the original crew's DNA. This one's for him, for the era, and for knowing when to stop.

🍿 Nolan clocks in at 2h 52m. For Homer's epic, that's actually... restrained. 📆 Estreno: July 17, 2026 🎭 Género: #Action · #Adventure · #Fantasy ✈️ Add to watchlist Nolan had already confirmed The Odyssey would be shorter than Oppenheimer. Most people braced for something around 2h20m. Getting 172 minutes on a mythic epic crossing the Mediterranean is genuinely surprising, and I mean that as a compliment. The guy who made Dunkirk run just 106 minutes and still make it feel enormous knows exactly what he's doing with a runtime. Nolan doesn't pad; he compresses. At $250 million and shot entirely on IMAX 70mm film cameras, this already feels like a once-in-a-generation swing. Matt Damon as Odysseus, and I'm genuinely intrigued.

🎬 Garry Watson , last silent film actor, is gone at 97 He debuted on screen at the age of one in the 1929 film Drag, the youngest of nine siblings who collectively appeared in over a thousand Hollywood productions. He is particularly recognized for his appearance in Frank Capra's Mr. Smith Goes to Washington , but his real distinction was simply outlasting everyone else. The silent era ran from roughly 1896 until The Jazz Singer (1927), with American cinema fully transitioning to sound by 1929. Worth noting: Watson was a one-year-old on set, not a craftsman of the form. But that's the point. All of the last surviving silent actors were child actors. The true artists of that era are long gone. What dies with Watson is the last living breath of contact, however fragile, with a cinema that moved without sound.

🎬 A 90-second ghost from 1921 that animation forgot 📆 Estreno: 1921 (fragment; never officially released) 🎭 Género: #Animation · #LostFilm · #SilentEra ✈️ Add to watchlist Winsor McCay , the man who gave us Gertie the Dinosaur , spent years animating centaurs onto live-action forest footage. Production notes say the finished footage amounted to over three minutes; only 90 seconds survive. The rest deteriorated into dust from negligent storage. What gets me is the audacity of the craft. McCay's fine linework and naturalistic style visibly influenced Disney's centaurs in Fantasia, twenty years later. And yet this thing was never released. Why it was abandoned remains unclear, though budgetary pressure and being pushed out of animation by Hearst may have played a role. Oh, and that male centaur throwing a rock at a random bird for zero reason? Absolute cinema.

🍿 ‘Street Fighter’ is shaping up to be the most wildly fun ride of the year 📆 Release : October 16, 2026 🎭 Genre : #Action · #MartialArts ✈️ Add movie This trailer won me over for one very simple reason... it understands the franchise doesn’t need to take itself too seriously to work. Kitao Sakurai, director of ‘ Bad Trip ’, dives headfirst into color, excess, and that pure ‘90s arcade spirit, with a chaotic Ken played by Noah Centineo (‘ The Recruit ’) and a rock-solid Ryu from Andrew Koji ( ‘Warrior’ ). What I love most is that it fully embraces its craziest side. Jason Momoa as Blanka, 50 Cent as Balrog, and David Dastmalchian (‘ The Suicide Squad’ ) as M. Bison. Sure, the trailer gives away a bit too much and I’m not expecting a particularly tight script, but if the fights deliver and it keeps that playful, over-the-top tone, this could be one of those delightfully dumb movies you enjoy with a grin from start to finish.

🍿 'Dune: Part Three' explodes: IMAX tickets sold out in minutes… 7 months early! 📆 Release date: December 18, 2026 🎭 Genre: #SciFi · #Epic ✈️ Add movie The hype for 'Dune: Part Three' is absolutely massive. The first batch of IMAX 70mm tickets, limited to just one daily screening in select theaters, sold out within minutes. In London, they lasted less than 10 minutes, and in other cities websites crashed, leaving many fans empty-handed. 🤯 What’s most striking is that these tickets went on sale seven months in advance… and people are already planning trips to other cities just to experience it in 70mm. Very few films generate this level of anticipation. 'Dune' is already playing in the league of true cinematic events. 🍿

🍿 'Dune: Part Three' promises the wildest chapter yet: Villeneuve hits the gas and Pattinson arrives like a desert demon 📆 Release : December 18, 2026 🎭 Genre : #ScienceFiction · #Thriller I’m completely sold on Denis Villeneuve’s vision: if the first film was contemplative and the second was a war movie, 'Dune: Part Three' wants to be a full-on thriller, tighter, more physical, and far more brutal. ⚔️ 🌵 The story jumps ahead 17 years and puts Paul Atreides face-to-face with the consequences of his power, with Chani once again at the emotional center of it all. What grabbed me most about the first trailer is its almost feverish energy: Timothée Chalamet radiates a deeply unsettling darkness, Zendaya looks set to have far more weight than Chani had in the book, and Robert Pattinson shows up as Scytale with a truly disturbing presence, somewhere between an albino messiah and an impossible villain. 😵‍💫 On top of that, Hans Zimmer once again turns Arrakis into the kind of IMAX experience that leaves you completely drained.

🍿 Cliff Booth is back, and it doesn’t feel like a fever dream 📆 Release : Coming soon 🎭 Genre : #Drama · #Thriller · #Hollywood ✈️ Add movie Netflix 📺 dropped the teaser for The Adventures of Cliff Booth during the Super Bowl, and it’s still hard to believe this is real. Brad Pitt returns to the role that earned him an Oscar in Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood, this time front and center and firmly set in the 1970s. The real power move isn’t the comeback itself, but who’s behind it: David Fincher ( Se7en , Fight Club ) directing a script by Quentin Tarantin o. A bizarre pairing… and a dangerously compelling one. The footage hints at a darker Cliff, less nostalgia, more grit: bars, racing, playful censorship, implied violence, and a less romanticized Hollywood. Fincher runs Tarantino’s universe through his cold, surgical lens, and that could be gold or pure dynamite, but it won’t be boring. Netflix going all in? Massive budget, a Super Bowl teaser, and an iconic character back behind the wheel. This feels like a high-end cinephile indulgence 🎬 🔥 .

🍿 🍿 'Lord of the Flies': BBC adapts Golding's most disturbing classic 📆 Release : February 8, 2026 (UK) 🎭 Genre : #Drama · #Thriller ✈️ Add to watchlist Jack Thorne (' Adolescence ') and Marc Munden turn William Golding's novel into a four-episode miniseries. British schoolboys stranded on an island with no adults, order crumbling into tribalism and violence. The timeless classic, but with a cast of over 30 young actors and a killer soundtrack: Cristobal Tapia de Veer (' The White Lotus ') scores the series while Hans Zimmer (' Dune ') composed the main theme 🎼 . The trailer already nails that suffocating atmosphere the material demands. If they captured the descent into chaos and loss of innocence right, this could be the best adaptation yet. 'Yellowjackets' fans, mark your calendars 🐚 🔥 .

🍿 Yoshi steps into the spotlight… and Nintendo hits the fan-service accelerator 📆 Release : April 1, 2026 🎭 Genre : #Animation · #Adventure · #Fantasy ✈️ Add to watchlist First look at Yoshi in The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, and the character works 🦖 … he doesn’t speak, he just grunts, and that’s the right call. It stays true to the games and avoids turning him into yet another chatty Illumination mascot. The trailer once again feels more Odyssey than Galaxy, leaning heavily on a parade of references: Birdo, Mouser, babies, power-up suits, a T-Rex… too much at once 🎮 The classic music does peek through, but I still doubt it’ll be respected all the way through 🎶 . There’s potential, sure, but also the sense that this franchise may be getting overloaded a bit too fast.

Sesame Street just got a massive free upgrade . YouTube is now the biggest digital library for the show, with 100+ full episodes available to stream for free on the Sesame Street and Sesame Street Classics channels. ☀️ And it’s not filler content. We’re talking iconic episodes like the 1969 premiere , “Goodbye Mr. Hooper,” and other classics that haven’t been this easy to watch on streaming. If you grew up with it, this is pure nostalgia. If you didn’t, this is the best possible starting point. 📺

🍿 ‘Crime 101’: the perfect heist on L.A.’s asphalt veins 📆 Release : February 13, 2026 🎭 Genre : #Thriller · #Crime ✈️ Add to watchlist What really grabs me about ‘Crime 101’ is its confidence. This looks like a sleek, old-school heist thriller, soaked in sun, concrete and quiet obsession. Chris Hemsworth ( ‘Thor’ , ‘Extraction’ ) dials down the superhero swagger and plays it cool as an elusive jewel thief who treats Los Angeles like a chessboard. He’s restrained, methodical, and surprisingly convincing in this colder register 💎 🚔 Mark Ruffalo ( ‘Zodiac’ , ‘Spotlight’ ) is right at home as a dogged detective convinced there’s a hidden pattern everyone else is missing. Halle Berry ( ‘Monster’s Ball’ , ‘ Die another day ’) brings real weight and allure as a disillusioned insurance broker standing at a personal breaking point. And whenever Barry Keoghan (‘T he Banshees of Inisherin ’, ‘Saltburn’ ) shows up, you know trouble isn’t far behind. Bart Layton, coming off the brilliant ‘American Animals’ , clearly understands the anatomy of obsession and risk. There’s a strong modern ‘Heat’ energy here 🔥 . Yes, the trailer might reveal a bit too much, but I’ll gladly take that if it means this kind of adult, theatrical crime film is back on the big screen. Stylish, tense, and refreshingly cinematic 🎬 .

🍿 ‘The Death of Robin Hood’: Hugh Jackman, A24’s Cursed Outlaw 📆 Release : 2026 (date TBA) 🎭 Genre : #Drama · #Action · #MedievalWestern ✈️ Add to watchlist Forget the green tights and merry forests. Hugh Jackman steps into the boots of a disillusioned outlaw, think Logan or Unforgiven , not the classic folk hero. Directed by Michael Sarnoski ( Pig , A Quiet Place: Day One ), this dark reimagining of the myth paints Robin Hood as a man broken by violence, seeking redemption through the hands of a mysterious woman (the always magnetic Jodie Comer). The trailer teases a raw, brutal aesthetic with the visual grit of The Northman and the tragic weight of a twilight epic. Jackman is nearly unrecognizable, aged, haunted, and already being whispered about in early Oscar conversations. Personally, I’m drawn to this somber twist. Sometimes, you need to drag a legend through the mud to find its humanity. And if A24 is giving us a Robin Hood who bleeds, kills, and regrets... I want to watch him burn. 🏹 🔥

🎬 Plot twist in Hollywood’s big merger drama. Warner Bros. Discovery has officially told Paramount “no thanks,” calling its latest $30-per-share takeover bid riskier and worse than the merger Warner already signed with Netflix. 💰 The Netflix deal : cash + stock, fewer strings, fewer financing headaches. 💣 The Paramount deal : massive debt, complex financing, and huge breakup costs if it collapses. WBD says the risk could blow a $4.7B hole in its balance sheet. Paramount’s counter-argument is simple: regulators will block Netflix first. Warner isn’t buying that either, saying both paths face similar approval risks. So for now: Netflix + Warner Bros. is still the preferred future. Paramount is stuck outside, knocking louder every week. Hollywood consolidation season is getting spicy.

🍿 ‘Scream 7’: Sidney Prescott Back in the Crosshairs — and Ghostface Is Ready to Burn It All Down 🔪 🔥 📆 Release : February 27, 2026 🎭 #Horror · #Slasher ✈️ Follow the movie Neve Campbell is back. Kevin Williamson (the guy who wrote the rules of the slasher with Scream (1996)) is now in charge. The trailer opens with the line that made us all addicted to late-night phone calls: ‘Hello, Sidney… did you miss me?’. With that alone, the fandom lost its mind. Sidney now lives a quiet life with her teenage daughter (Isabel May) and her cop husband (Joel McHale). Quiet, until Ghostface dials her number again. The trailer makes it clear that this time, the killer isn’t just after blood — he wants to erase the legend. And yes, someone screams ‘I’m gonna burn it all down’ as the Macher house goes up in flames. 🔥 We see Courteney Cox again and, surprise, even the “dead” Matthew Lillard and Skeet Ulrich return. But fans are divided: some are celebrating Sidney’s comeback, while others say the franchise has lost its meta edge and now feels more like Halloween (2018) than Scream 4 . To me, it’s obvious. It’s bloody fan service — an emotional farewell soaked in nostalgia with a hint of unintentional self-parody. Cringe, chaos, and stab wounds. Exactly how it should be. 🩸

🎃 ‘South Park’ blows up the White House… and Trump The new Halloween special, ‘The Woman in the Hat’, is pure dynamite 💥 . Trump decides to demolish the East Wing of the White House to build a ballroom, while a ghost slips in through the rubble and Stan starts wondering if South Park has become too political. I love seeing the return of that furious South Park, the one that doesn’t forgive anyone, not even itself. Sure, many fans miss the boys’ classic crazy adventures, but let’s be honest: watching Trump and Satan oversee a presidential demolition sounds way too fun to complain 😈 . 🤯 12 MOVIES WITH TWIST ENDINGS THAT WILL BLOW YOUR MIND (and that you’ll never see the same way twice) 🎬 Some movies don’t just end — they hit you. The kind that make you stare at the credits in total silence, replaying everything in your head. Here are 12 films that completely change once you know the ending — and experiencing them for the first time is pure cinematic magic. 1️⃣ The Usual Suspects (1995) A police interrogation, a mysterious criminal, and the most iconic reveal in modern cinema 🕵️‍♂️ . Kevin Spacey earned his Oscar — but the real winner is the audience’s disbelief. 2️⃣ The Sixth Sense (1999) ‘I see dead people.’ 👻 M. Night Shyamalan redefined the plot twist with a finale that’s still unmatched 25 years later. 3️⃣ The Others (2001) Nicole Kidman shines in this elegant ghost story with a twist that chills to the bone ❄️ . Atmospheric, haunting, and beautifully tragic. 4️⃣ Memento (2000) Christopher Nolan tells the story backwards 🌀 — and leaves your brain scrambled. When it ends, you’ll want to start over… literally. 5️⃣ The Prestige (2006) Two magicians, one deadly obsession, and a reveal that hurts more than a knife 🎩 . Bale vs. Jackman in a duel for the ages. 6️⃣ Fight Club (1999) I can’t talk about it — but let’s just say its twist changed late-’90s cinema forever 💥 . Tyler Durden still lives rent-free in our heads. 7️⃣ Shutter Island (2010) Scorsese and DiCaprio mess with your mind until you can’t tell what’s real 🧠 . That ending? Equal parts brilliant and devastating. 🎥 Some — like Memento or Arrival — get even better when you know the ending. But others — The Sixth Sense, Oldboy, Primal Fear — you can only truly experience once. And that first time… is cinematic perfection. 👀 Click here to see the full list...

🍿 ‘Tim Burton: Life in the Line’ – The Gothic Genius Unmasked 🕯 🎩 📆 Premiere : October 23, 2025 🎭 Genre : #Documentary · #Biography ✈️ Follow documentary Tara Wood —the filmmaker behind ‘QT8: The First Eight’ and ‘21 Years: Richard Linklater’— now dives into the most poetic and shadowy corner of cinema: Tim Burton’s world. ‘Tim Burton: Life in the Line’ is a four-part docuseries tracing his journey from his misfit days at Disney to the triumphs of ‘Batman’ (1989), ‘Edward Scissorhands’, and ‘The Nightmare Before Christmas’, all the way to his comeback with Netflix’s ‘Wednesday’. 🦇 ✨ The project promises unseen footage, rare sketches, and intimate testimonies from Burton’s closest collaborators: Johnny Depp, Winona Ryder, Helena Bonham Carter, Michael Keaton, Danny Elfman, and Jenna Ortega among others. It’s a gathering of kindred spirits who help decode the mind of cinema’s most beloved outsider —the man who turned weirdness into beauty. For me, what’s truly captivating is how this docuseries seems to reconcile Burton the man with Burton the myth. Some may say we already know his story, but his universe still pulses between melancholy and imagination. And yes… I’ll always dream of that Batman trilogy we never got. 🖤 🎬

🍿 ‘Primate’: The Killer Ape Hollywood Has Been Afraid to Make 🐒 🔪 📆 Release : January 9, 2026 🎭 Genre : #Horror · #DarkComedy ✈️ Follow movie Johannes Roberts ( 47 Meters Down , The Strangers: Prey at Night ) directs this story about a group of friends enjoying a tropical getaway—until their family pet, a chimp named Ben, goes berserk after being bitten by something mysterious. What follows is ninety minutes of chaos, screams, and blood under the Hawaiian sun. ☀️ 💉 The trailer leans into the same absurd horror vibe that made M3GAN a hit and clearly nods to the chimp scene from Nope . The blend of terror and comedy is so shameless you’re never sure whether to laugh or hide behind your hands. A brutal warning about human arrogance in trying to tame the wild… yet also proof that watching a monkey unlock a car with a key fob can be terrifyingly fun. 🧠 💀

🍿 ‘Send Help’: Sam Raimi Turns a Deserted Island into a Psychological Battlefield 🌴 💀 📆 Release : January 30, 2026 🎭 Genre : #Horror · #DarkComedy · #PsychologicalThriller ✈️ Follow movie Sam Raimi —the mastermind behind The Evil Dead and the original Spider-Man trilogy— returns to his wildest roots with Send Help, his first non-franchise horror film since Drag Me to Hell . Rachel McAdams ( Spotlight , Mean Girls ) stars as Linda, an underappreciated employee stranded on an island with her boss from hell, Bradley (Dylan O’Brien, The Maze Runner ), after surviving a plane crash. What begins as a survival story quickly turns into a darkly funny, blood-soaked power struggle for dominance. What fascinates me most is how Raimi flips the hierarchy: the underdog becomes the predator 💪 . Many are calling it a mix between Misery , Cast Away , and Triangle of Sadness —but with Raimi’s signature flair: grotesque, frantic, and wickedly fun. McAdams promises a full-on “Regina George in survival mode” performance, and that alone is worth the ticket. Raimi is back, and horror is groovy again.

🍿 ‘Young Washington’: the hero who started a war before starting his own 🇺🇸 🔥 📆 Release : July 3, 2026 🎭 Genre : #Historical · #Drama · #Biopic ✈️ Follow movie Angel Studios is getting ahead of the U.S. Semiquincentennial with a lavish production that aims to turn young George Washington into the new icon of cinematic patriotism. Directed by Jon Erwin (‘ The Jesus Revolution ’), the film portrays the future president —played by William Franklyn-Miller— in the midst of the French and Indian War, surrounded by gunpowder, mud, and choices that would shape a continent. 💥 The trailer promises epic scale, faith, and fiery speeches, but it smells more like ‘The Patriot’ than a history lesson. With Mary-Louise Parker, Kelsey Grammer, Andy Serkis, and Ben Kingsley rounding out the cast, the film is clearly aiming to repeat the box-office miracle of ‘ Sound of Freedom ’ —though many are already raising an eyebrow at the Angel Studios label: propaganda wrapped in glossy celluloid. Personally, I’m curious to see how they’ll polish (or not) the image of a reckless, slave-owning Washington who helped ignite a war. It may end up being a patriotic version of Young Hercules, but I have to admit — the historical intrigue is definitely there. ⚔️

🍿 Steve: Cillian Murphy against the system and his own demons 📆 Premiere : October 3, 2025 (Netflix) 🎭 Genre : #Drama · #ComingOfAge ✈️ Follow movie 📺 What a delight to see Cillian Murphy in such a raw and fragile role after the whirlwind of Oppenheimer . Here, he reunites with Tim Mielants ( Small Things Like These ) to portray the headmaster of a reform school in the ’90s, a worn-out man fighting against the institution’s imminent closure while battling his own inner struggles. Opposite him, Jay Lycurgo ( Last Swim ) plays Shy, a teenager caught between the violence of his past and the uncertainty of his future. Director Mielants really convinces here, having worked with the boys in intensive workshops so that their real lives would bleed into their characters. 🎬 The score by Ben Salisbury and Geoff Barrow promises that electrifying yet sensitive touch that always hooks me. Behind its simple title lies a complex portrait of forgotten youth, education as refuge, and the power of not having to face life alone.

🍿 Frankenstein: Guillermo del Toro’s Most Anticipated Monster 📆 Release : October 17 in theaters · November 7 on Netflix 🎭 Genre : #Drama · #Horror · #SciFi ✈️ Follow movie After more than three decades reinventing the figure of the monster (from The Devil’s Backbone to The Shape of Water ), Guillermo del Toro is finally taking on the mother of all stories: Frankenstein. Oscar Isaac plays Victor Frankenstein and Jacob Elordi surprises as the Creature, built from the remains of Crimean War soldiers, in a version as melancholic as it is brutal. Mia Goth, Christoph Waltz, and Charles Dance round out a cast that screams awards season gold. ⚡️ Del Toro has also addressed a long-pending matter in his career: his dreamed adaptation of At the Mountains of Madness , H. P. Lovecraft’s famous novella. It was one of his most personal projects and he spent more than a decade trying to make it happen with James Cameron as producer, but studios always considered it too expensive and too adult. Now the director admits he won’t pursue it anymore, leaving it as the great impossible film of his career. I’ve watched the trailer several times and, although some shots carry that divisive “Netflix look” 📺 , I can’t deny there are images that burn into your mind (that angel of death or the monster capsizing a ship are pure del Toro iconography). 🖤
